_about: How published frameworks INFORM this research prototype. The 'published concept' column summarises the frameworks from general knowledge; the official texts (ITIL 4 publications, ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018, ISO 10002:2018) were NOT accessed and should be checked before citing. The project claims no compliance, certification or official approval.

frameworks.name: ITIL 4 (AXELOS / PeopleCert, 2019)
frameworks.published_concept: Incident management practice: incidents are prioritised from their impact and urgency so that the most damaging ones are handled first; service level management sets agreed targets.
frameworks.used_for: Agent 2 derives priority from an Impact x Urgency matrix; Agent 3 attaches simulated response and resolution targets to tickets.
frameworks.custom: The impact and urgency rules, the three levels, the matrix cells and the SLA hours are this project's own design.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 — Service management system requirements
frameworks.published_concept: Requirements for a service management system, including incident management, service requests, service level management and continual improvement, with recorded and traceable decisions.
frameworks.used_for: Every classification, prioritisation, routing and escalation decision is recorded in an audit trail; insights feed improvement.
frameworks.custom: No management system, certification or audit is implemented; the prototype only borrows the principle of documented, traceable handling.

frameworks.name: ISO 10002:2018 — Guidelines for complaints handling in organizations
frameworks.published_concept: Guiding principles for complaints handling such as visibility, accessibility, responsiveness, objectivity, confidentiality, a customer-focused approach, accountability and continual improvement.
frameworks.used_for: Agent 3 acknowledges each piece of feedback with a reply draft, asks for missing details, decides from evidence, checks prior complaints before escalation, and keeps decisions accountable through human review.
frameworks.custom: The reply templates, the escalation rules E1–E5 and the routing to handling teams are research-defined.

frameworks.name: EGSQUAL (Aljukhadar et al., 2022)
frameworks.published_concept: A validated survey scale of e-government website service quality with seven dimensions.
frameworks.used_for: Agent 1 maps each issue to a service-quality category with a provisional EGSQUAL dimension.
frameworks.custom: Using the scale as a coding frame for Arabic app reviews, the categories and the crosswalk are this project's adaptation (see the EGSQUAL section).

human_in_the_loop: Every simulated ticket, escalation recommendation and Arabic reply draft is a recommendation for a human officer.
No external escalation happens without explicit human approval (rule E5); escalation is simulated and nothing is sent to AMER, the DGA or any government system.
Complaint numbers, dates and statuses are never invented: missing details lead to a request for information or PENDING_VERIFICATION.
LLM failures fall back to transparent rules and are flagged on the result.
Severity, priority and escalation rules are research proposals that a service owner would have to review before any real use.
